claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a solid solution.
The as-synthesized catalyst exhibits inherent tensile lattice strain.
Controlled thermal annealing can reduce lattice strain while maintaining particle size and compositional homogeneity.
Relief of tensile lattice strain causes a downward shift of the surface-atom d-band center.
A downward shift of the d-band center weakens adsorption of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Weaker binding of ethanol-oxidation intermediates alters the reaction pathway and product selectivity.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit a shift in ethanol-oxidation onset potential relative to the as-synthesized catalyst.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit an altered product distribution relative to the as-synthesized catalyst.
Annealing may increase formation of partial ethanol-oxidation products.
Annealing may improve durability if it stabilizes the active surface structure.
The proposed behavior is expected under ethanol oxidation in acidic electrolyte at 50–80 °C with controlled potential cycling.
The proposed mechanism is conditional on annealing not inducing phase segregation or significant particle-morphology changes.
The as-synthesized catalyst in its native strain state is the experimental baseline.
The hypothesis is falsified if annealing produces no measurable downward d-band-center shift or no statistically significant activity or selectivity difference from the baseline.
